results.Summary: Southeast Toyota Distributors, LLC (SET) is recalling certain 2017-2019 Toyota Camry, Corolla, Rav4, Sienna, and Yaris iA vehicles equipped with factory-installed floor mats. As such, these vehicles fail to comply with the requirements of Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) number 110, "Tire Selection and Rims."

results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Summary: Toyota Motor Engineering & Manufacturing (Toyota) is recalling certain 2019 Camry vehicles. The Occupant Classification System (OCS) may have been improperly calibrated, which may prevent the proper deployment of the front passenger air bag and knee air bag, in the event of a crash. results.Remedy: Toyota will notify owners, and dealers will recalibrate the OCS, free of charge.  The recall began August 27, 2019.  Owners may contact Toyota customer service at 1-888-270-9371.  Toyota's number for this recall is K0M.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

Because the recall remedy had not been performed prior to the loss date, a product-liability subrogation theory against Toyota is supported: had the defect been remediated, the brake failure and resulting collision may have been prevented. The rules engine confirms the recall match, calculates a net demand of $6,900 after applying the 40% comparative fault reduction under Texas's modified 51% rule (insured fault does not bar recovery), and shows 531 days remaining before the statute-of-limitations deadline — making timely pursuit both viable and warranted.

risks.detail: Toyota will argue that the insured's 40% comparative fault (e.g., following distance, speed, inattention) was the primary or superseding cause of the collision, not the brake defect, and may retain an accident-reconstruction expert to support that theory.

Toyota may contend that NHTSA recall notices were mailed to the registered owner and that the vehicle owner's failure to schedule the free remedy constitutes an intervening act that breaks the causal chain between the manufacturer's defect and the loss.

risks.risk: Pre-existing brake wear or maintenance neglect
risks.detail: Defense counsel will likely subpoena maintenance records and argue that worn brake components, low brake fluid, or deferred service — rather than the recall defect — caused the pedal failure, shifting liability to the vehicle owner or a third-party repair shop.

Without a post-loss inspection report or expert affidavit confirming the vacuum assist failure as the proximate cause, Toyota can challenge the causal link as speculative; securing a forensic mechanical inspection of the brake system before the SOL deadline (531 days) is critical to strengthening the demand.

risks.risk: Comparative fault bar risk under Texas modified 51% rule
risks.detail: Although the insured's current fault allocation of 40% does not bar recovery, Toyota will attempt to shift additional fault to the insured during litigation; if fault is re-apportioned to 51% or more, recovery is completely barred under Texas law.
